questions.stem: This schematic traces how blood cells arise from a common precursor and mature through the bone marrow, blood, and tissue compartments. In aplastic anemia, loss of which population at the top of this scheme accounts for the pancytopenia?

explanation.summary: The diagram shows a multipotent stem cell giving rise to myeloid and lymphoid lineages. Aplastic anemia results from destruction of the myeloid hematopoietic stem cells, so RBCs, platelets, granulocytes, and monocytes all fall while lymphocytes (lymphoid-derived) are relatively spared.
explanation.whyCorrect: The diagram shows a multipotent stem cell giving rise to myeloid and lymphoid lineages. Aplastic anemia results from destruction of the myeloid hematopoietic stem cells, so RBCs, platelets, granulocytes, and monocytes all fall while lymphocytes (lymphoid-derived) are relatively spared.

questions.stem: These images depict the six maturation stages of a granulocyte. At which point in this sequence does the cell lose its ability to divide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the myeloblast stage, before any granules appear

choices.label: B
choices.text: It continues to divide at every stage until it is fully segmented

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the band stage, just before nuclear segmentation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only the final segmented cell retains the ability to divide

choices.label: E
choices.text: At the metamyelocyte stage; cells beyond the myelocyte no longer divide

explanation.summary: Neutrophil precursors proliferate through the myeloblast, promyelocyte, and myelocyte stages. Once the cell reaches the metamyelocyte stage it can no longer divide and only matures (nuclear indentation to band, then segmentation).
explanation.whyCorrect: Neutrophil precursors proliferate through the myeloblast, promyelocyte, and myelocyte stages. Once the cell reaches the metamyelocyte stage it can no longer divide and only matures (nuclear indentation to band, then segmentation).

questions.stem: Several abnormal red cell forms are labeled on this blood smear (schistocytes, triangulocytes, helmet cells). What single event produces all of these shapes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shearing of red cells by intravascular microthrombi

choices.label: B
choices.text: A hereditary defect in membrane spectrin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Splenic macrophage digestion of red cell membrane

explanation.summary: Helmet cells, triangulocytes, and other schistocyte forms all arise from mechanical fragmentation as red cells pass fibrin strands and microthrombi, so they share the same microangiopathic origin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Helmet cells, triangulocytes, and other schistocyte forms all arise from mechanical fragmentation as red cells pass fibrin strands and microthrombi, so they share the same microangiopathic origin.

questions.stem: This figure compares lymphocyte morphology across three fields: a small round cell in panel A versus the larger, more irregular and voluminous cells in panels B and C. Cells like those in B and C are best described as what?

explanation.summary: Panel A shows normal-appearing lymphocytes, as seen when a benign lymphocytosis increases normal cells. Panels B and C show reactive lymphocytes, which are larger with more voluminous, sometimes deeply basophilic cytoplasm and are typical of viral infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Panel A shows normal-appearing lymphocytes, as seen when a benign lymphocytosis increases normal cells. Panels B and C show reactive lymphocytes, which are larger with more voluminous, sometimes deeply basophilic cytoplasm and are typical of viral infection.
